front: Il faut que tu viennes ce soir.
pronunciation: [eel foh kuh tü VYEN suh SWAHR]
back: You have to come tonight.
context: Subjunctive after 'il faut que'. Form: 'ils' present stem + -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent (ils viennent → que tu viennes).

front: Je veux que tu me dises la vérité.
pronunciation: [zhuh vuh kuh tü muh deez lah vay-ree-TAY]
back: I want you to tell me the truth.
context: Will/wish + que + subjunctive when the subjects differ.

front: Je veux te dire la vérité.
pronunciation: [zhuh vuh tuh deer lah vay-ree-TAY]
back: I want to tell you the truth.
context: Same subject → infinitive, never 'je veux que je dise'.

front: J'aimerais qu'il fasse beau demain.
pronunciation: [zheh-muh-reh keel fas BOH duh-MAN]
back: I'd like the weather to be nice tomorrow.
context: 'Faire' → que je fasse, que nous fassions.

front: Il est important que vous soyez à l'heure.
pronunciation: [ee leh tan-por-tahn kuh voo swah-YAY ah LUHR]
back: It's important that you be on time.
context: 'Être' → que je sois, tu sois, il soit, nous soyons, vous soyez, ils soient.

front: Je suis content que tu aies réussi.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee kohn-tahn kuh tü EH ray-ü-SEE]
back: I'm glad you succeeded.
context: Past subjunctive: que + subjunctive of avoir/être + participle. 'Avoir' → que j'aie, tu aies, il ait…

front: Je doute qu'il puisse venir.
pronunciation: [zhuh doot keel PWEES vuh-NEER]
back: I doubt he can come.
context: 'Pouvoir' → que je puisse.

front: Il est possible qu'elle sache la réponse.
pronunciation: [ee leh poh-see-bluh kel SASH lah ray-POHNS]
back: It's possible she knows the answer.
context: 'Savoir' → que je sache.

front: Je ne crois pas qu'il ait raison.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh krwah pah keel eh reh-ZOHN]
back: I don't think he's right.
context: Negative opinion → subjunctive. Compare 'je crois qu'il a raison' (indicative).

front: Crois-tu qu'il vienne ?
pronunciation: [krwah-TÜ keel VYEN]
back: Do you think he'll come?
context: Inverted opinion questions can take the subjunctive (formal); in speech 'tu crois qu'il va venir ?' is more common.

front: Bien qu'il soit fatigué, il continue à travailler.
pronunciation: [byan keel swah fah-tee-GAY, eel kohn-tee-nü ah trah-vah-YAY]
back: Although he's tired, he keeps working.
context: 'Bien que' (although) always takes the subjunctive.

front: Quoi qu'elle dise, je ne la crois pas.
pronunciation: [kwah-kel DEEZ, zhuh nuh lah krwah PAH]
back: Whatever she says, I don't believe her.
context: 'Quoi que' (two words) = whatever; 'quoique' (one word) = although. Both + subjunctive.

front: Je te prête ma voiture pour que tu puisses aller au travail.
pronunciation: [zhuh tuh pret mah vwah-TÜR poor kuh tü pwees ah-lay oh trah-VAHY]
back: I'm lending you my car so that you can get to work.
context: 'Pour que' (so that) + subjunctive.

front: Parle plus fort afin que tout le monde t'entende.
pronunciation: [parl plü FOR ah-fan kuh tool mohnd tahn-TAHND]
back: Speak louder so that everyone can hear you.
context: 'Afin que' = so that (more formal).

front: Pars avant qu'il ne soit trop tard.
pronunciation: [par ah-vahn keel nuh swah troh TAR]
back: Leave before it's too late.
context: 'Avant que' + subjunctive, often with a 'ne explétif' (not a negation).

front: Attends jusqu'à ce que je revienne.
pronunciation: [ah-tahn zhüs-kah suh kuh zhuh ruh-VYEN]
back: Wait until I come back.
context: 'Jusqu'à ce que' = until + subjunctive.

front: Je t'aide à condition que tu m'aides aussi.
pronunciation: [zhuh ted ah kohn-dee-syohn kuh tü med oh-SEE]
back: I'll help you on condition that you help me too.
context: 'À condition que' = provided that + subjunctive.

front: Il est parti sans que personne ne le remarque.
pronunciation: [ee leh par-tee sahn kuh pehr-sun nuh luh ruh-MARK]
back: He left without anyone noticing.
context: 'Sans que' + subjunctive.

front: À moins qu'il pleuve, on ira à la plage.
pronunciation: [ah mwan keel PLUHV, ohn nee-rah ah lah PLAZH]
back: Unless it rains, we'll go to the beach.
context: 'À moins que' = unless + subjunctive.

front: J'ai peur qu'il ne soit déjà trop tard.
pronunciation: [zhay puhr keel nuh swah day-zhah troh TAR]
back: I'm afraid it may already be too late.
context: Fear + subjunctive, often with 'ne explétif' in careful French.

front: Je suis désolé que tu sois malade.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee day-zoh-lay kuh tü swah mah-LAD]
back: I'm sorry you're ill.
context: Emotion + que + subjunctive.

front: C'est dommage qu'il ne puisse pas venir.
pronunciation: [seh doh-mahzh keel nuh pwees pah vuh-NEER]
back: It's a shame he can't come.
context: 'C'est dommage que' + subjunctive.

front: Je m'étonne qu'elle n'ait rien dit.
pronunciation: [zhuh may-tun kel neh ryan DEE]
back: I'm surprised she didn't say anything.
context: Surprise + subjunctive (past).

front: Il vaut mieux que tu restes à la maison.
pronunciation: [eel voh myuh kuh tü rest ah lah meh-ZOHN]
back: You'd better stay home.
context: 'Il vaut mieux que' + subjunctive.

front: Il est nécessaire que nous prenions une décision.
pronunciation: [ee leh nay-seh-sehr kuh noo pruh-nyohn ün day-see-ZYOHN]
back: It's necessary that we make a decision.
context: 'Prendre' → que nous prenions (nous form uses the nous stem).

front: Je souhaite que vous passiez de bonnes fêtes.
pronunciation: [zhuh swet kuh voo pah-syay duh bun FET]
back: I hope you have a lovely holiday season.
context: 'Souhaiter que' + subjunctive.

front: J'espère que vous passerez de bonnes fêtes.
pronunciation: [zheh-spehr kuh voo pahs-ray duh bun FET]
back: I hope you'll have a lovely holiday season.
context: Careful: 'espérer que' takes the INDICATIVE, unlike 'souhaiter que'.

front: Il faut que j'aille à la banque.
pronunciation: [eel foh kuh ZHAHY ah lah BAHNK]
back: I have to go to the bank.
context: 'Aller' → que j'aille, tu ailles, il aille, nous allions, vous alliez, ils aillent.

front: Je ne pense pas qu'ils veuillent venir.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh pahns pah keel VUHY vuh-NEER]
back: I don't think they want to come.
context: 'Vouloir' → qu'ils veuillent.

front: Qu'il entre !
pronunciation: [kee LAHNTR]
back: Let him come in!
context: Subjunctive as a third-person command.

front: Vive la France !
pronunciation: [veev lah FRAHNS]
back: Long live France!
context: A frozen subjunctive (que vive…). Also 'Vive les vacances !'

front: C'est le seul restaurant qui soit ouvert le lundi.
pronunciation: [seh luh suhl res-toh-rahn kee swah too-vehr luh lan-DEE]
back: It's the only restaurant that's open on Mondays.
context: After 'le seul', 'le premier', 'le dernier' + qui/que, the subjunctive is common.

front: Je cherche quelqu'un qui sache parler chinois.
pronunciation: [zhuh shersh kel-kan kee sash par-lay shee-NWAH]
back: I'm looking for someone who can speak Chinese.
context: Hypothetical person (may not exist) → subjunctive.

front: Je connais quelqu'un qui sait parler chinois.
pronunciation: [zhuh koh-neh kel-kan kee seh par-lay shee-NWAH]
back: I know someone who can speak Chinese.
context: Real, known person → indicative.

front: Bien que ce soit cher, ça vaut le coup.
pronunciation: [byan kuh suh swah SHEHR, sah voh luh KOO]
back: Although it's expensive, it's worth it.
context: 'Valoir le coup' = to be worth it.

front: Il faut qu'on se voie bientôt.
pronunciation: [eel foh kohn suh VWAH byan-TOH]
back: We have to see each other soon.
context: 'Voir' → que je voie, que nous voyions.

front: Je préfère que tu ne le saches pas.
pronunciation: [zhuh pray-fehr kuh tü nuh luh SASH pah]
back: I'd rather you didn't know.
context: 'Préférer que' + subjunctive.

front: Elle exige que tout soit parfait.
pronunciation: [el eg-zeezh kuh too swah par-FEH]
back: She demands that everything be perfect.
context: 'Exiger que' + subjunctive.

front: Il se peut que je sois en retard.
pronunciation: [eel suh puh kuh zhuh swah zahn ruh-TAR]
back: I may be late.
context: 'Il se peut que' + subjunctive = it may be that.

front: Il est temps que nous partions.
pronunciation: [ee leh TAHN kuh noo par-TYOHN]
back: It's time for us to leave.
context: 'Il est temps que' + subjunctive.

front: Que tu le veuilles ou non, tu viens avec nous.
pronunciation: [kuh tü luh VUHY oo NOHN, tü vyan ah-vek NOO]
back: Whether you like it or not, you're coming with us.
context: 'Que… ou non' = whether… or not + subjunctive.

front: Pourvu qu'il fasse beau ce week-end !
pronunciation: [poor-vü keel fas BOH suh wee-KEND]
back: Let's hope the weather's nice this weekend!
context: 'Pourvu que' = let's hope that / provided that + subjunctive.

front: Je ne suis pas certain que ce soit une bonne idée.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh swee pah sehr-tan kuh suh swah tün bun ee-DAY]
back: I'm not sure it's a good idea.
context: Uncertainty → subjunctive.

front: Il semble que la situation se soit améliorée.
pronunciation: [eel sahm-bluh kuh lah see-tü-ah-syohn suh swah tah-may-lyoh-RAY]
back: It seems the situation has improved.
context: 'Il semble que' + subjunctive; but 'il me semble que' + indicative.

front: Après qu'il est parti, tout le monde s'est détendu.
pronunciation: [ah-preh keel eh par-TEE, tool mohnd seh day-tahn-DÜ]
back: After he left, everyone relaxed.
context: Trap: 'après que' takes the INDICATIVE in correct French, though many natives use the subjunctive.
